summary: The team is pivoting global marketing toward China-based programs—Asia Star and Intelligent China—while juggling a knowledge website redesign and a nagging Outlook lockout that's blocking email access.
summaryDetail: The single most urgent item is the Outlook account lockout: the team must delete and re-add accounts, update the new password across laptops and phones, and confirm with CKGSB that the backend is unlocked before email work can resume. In parallel, the search/AI visibility strategy is now anchored on promoting Asia Star and the new Intelligent China as top priorities, with US partnerships (Stanford, Columbia, Berkeley) demoted to secondary—Joseph owes the target prompts document, customer profiles, and a conversion-tracking brief so the Google Ads audit can begin. The knowledge website redesign is moving forward: the team agreed to keep the two-menu structure, disperse videos by topic, and surface the BCI/BSI index banner, with Joseph sharing the HTML reference and a 30-minute feedback session needed before Joker makes changes. Looking ahead, the 2026 Women in Leadership Forum needs Ms. Kanta Singh formally invited, the Dean's letter must be printed and routed for signature, and the event page must be pushed to completion so GP, EMBA, and MBA outreach can go out.

decisions.text: Use the new password across all devices and update any device that changed passwords
Remove the standalone videos section and disperse videos by topic across the site.
Keep the two-menu structure (Knowledge menu and School menu) at the top.
Bring the BCI (and BSI) index banner into the knowledge section, similar to the school homepage.
Do not display a stock-market ticker at the very top of the homepage.
Prioritize Asia Star and Intelligent China as the top two programs to promote; US partnerships (Stanford, Columbia, Berkeley) are secondary.
Treat Berkeley as a possible third priority and include it in the audit phase.
Focus initial efforts on China-based programs given stronger demand from overseas executives.
